'''Suwa Shrine''' (諏訪神社) refers to shrines with "Suwa" in their name, particularly associated with {{ill|Suwa Shrine|ja|諏訪信仰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Faith|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 諏訪神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2370082}}, a form of {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|qid=Q812767|lt=Shinto}} worship centered on {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}}.

== Overview ==

There are approximately 25,000 Suwa Shrines throughout Japan, all having {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}} in Nagano Prefecture as their head shrine. Suwa Faith revolves around the veneration of {{ill|Takeminakata|en|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata}}, the main deity, and his consort {{ill|Yasakatome|en|Yasakatome|qid=Q9150392|lt=Yasakatome no Kami}}. Together, they are referred to as the "Suwa Deities" (諏訪大神). When Suwa Grand Shrine's deities are transferred to other Suwa Shrines, their divine spirits are believed to reside within a ritual {{ill|Nagi Kama|ja|薙鎌}}, which becomes the sacred object of the shrine.

Suwa Grand Shrine conducts the renowned {{ill|Onbashira|en|Onbashira|qid=Q3698846|lt=Onbashira Festival}}, held every six years. Many Suwa Shrines across the country host similar festivals. Additionally, rituals like the spring {{ill|Ontōsai|ja|御頭祭}} and {{ill|Misayama Festival|ja|御射山祭}}, a traditional hunting ceremony in late August, are celebrated at various Suwa Shrines.
